title: Pattern-anodyne inclusions detect fibered objects and are trivial cofibrations
statement:
Let $P=(B,S,\{p_a:K_a^{\triangleleft}\to B\}_{a\in A})$ be a small categorical pattern of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], with every $2$-simplex scaled. Use marked simplicial sets and $L^\flat,L^\sharp$ from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and the pattern model structure $\mathsf M_P$ of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus]. For $n\geq1$, $\Lambda_i^n\subseteq\Delta^n$ is the union of all faces except the $i$th, $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of all proper faces, and $L\star K$ denotes the simplicial join: its simplices are simplices of either factor and concatenations of a simplex of $L$ followed by a simplex of $K$. A subcomplex with an indicated marking is given the intersection marking unless otherwise specified.

Define a family $J_P$ of marked inclusions over $(B,S)$ by the following seven types, including every base map satisfying the conditions indicated:
(A0) $(\Lambda_1^2)^\sharp\amalg_{(\Lambda_1^2)^\flat}(\Delta^2)^\flat\longrightarrow(\Delta^2)^\sharp$, over every $\Delta^2\to B$ carrying all edges into $S$.
(A1) $Q^\flat\longrightarrow Q^\sharp$, where $Q=\Delta^0\amalg_{\Delta^{\{0,2\}}}\Delta^3\amalg_{\Delta^{\{1,3\}}}\Delta^0$ (both indicated edges are collapsed to vertices), over every $Q\to B$ carrying all edges into $S$.
(B0) $\{0\}^\sharp\longrightarrow(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, over every edge of $S$.
(B1) $K_a^\sharp\longrightarrow(K_a^{\triangleleft})^\sharp$, over $p_a$, for every $a\in A$.
(C0) $(\Lambda_0^n)^\flat\amalg_{(\Delta^{\{0,1\}})^\flat}(\Delta^{\{0,1\}})^\sharp\longrightarrow(\Delta^n)^\flat\amalg_{(\Delta^{\{0,1\}})^\flat}(\Delta^{\{0,1\}})^\sharp$, for every $n>1$ and every $\Delta^n\to B$ carrying the first edge into $S$.
(C1) $(\Lambda_i^n)^\flat\longrightarrow(\Delta^n)^\flat$, for $0<i<n$, over every $\Delta^n\to B$.
(C2) For $n\geq1$, $a\in A$ and every $f:\Delta^n\star K_a\to B$ restricting to $p_a$ on $\{n\}\star K_a$, take
$$ (\partial\Delta^n\star K_a)^\flat\amalg_{(\{n\}\star K_a)^\flat}(\{n\}\star K_a)^\sharp\longrightarrow(\Delta^n\star K_a)^\flat\amalg_{(\{n\}\star K_a)^\flat}(\{n\}\star K_a)^\sharp. $$

A marked object $X\to(B,S)$ is $P$-fibered if and only if each marked map $D\to X$ over $B$, for each $j:D\to E$ in $J_P$, extends to a marked map $E\to X$ over $B$. Every map in the weakly saturated class generated by $J_P$ is a trivial cofibration in $\mathsf M_P$. Here weakly saturated means closed under pushouts, small transfinite composites and retracts in the arrow category, and trivial cofibration means a cofibration which is a weak equivalence. These assertions hold in any fixed universe containing the pattern, without a finiteness assumption on the $K_a$.

source.place: Higher Algebra (September 18, 2017), Definition B.1.1 (A0,A1,B0,B1,C0,C1,C2), Proposition B.1.6, Proposition B.1.14 and Example B.2.2; printed pp.1470-1474,1481-1482. Restricted to fully scaled patterns over quasicategories. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag treats this infinity-categorical lifting calculus.

proof.text: Identify the family in the statement with $J_{\mathfrak P}$ of [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products], taking $C=B$ and $\mathfrak P=P$. The maps (A0), (A1), (B0), (B1), (C1) and (C2) have identical underlying maps, markings and allowed base maps. For (C0), the pushout marking adds exactly the edge $01$ and the degenerate edges, so it is precisely the notation $(U,\{01\})$ used there. This follows from the definition of a marking-preserving map: a map out of that pushout is an underlying map whose edge $01$ is marked. The join conventions agree by ordered concatenation. Thus the two families, and consequently their weakly saturated closures, coincide.

source.place: Definition B.1.1; comparison of the explicit generators with the existing DAG statement.

proof.text: Apply the fibered-object criterion in [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products] to this identified family. The terminal object in the slice is the identity of $(B,S)$. A square against the terminal map $X\to(B,S)$ consists exactly of a marked map $D\to X$ over $B$ and the already specified structural map $E\to(B,S)$. Its diagonal is precisely a marked extension $E\to X$ over $B$. The cited criterion therefore gives both directions of the first assertion, with exactly the extension property stated here.

source.place: Proposition B.1.6; its lifting characterization as recorded in the existing lifting-products node.

proof.text: Let $u:A\to A^{\prime}$ be any member of the weakly saturated closure of $J_P$, and let $Z$ be any $P$-fibered object. By the identification in step 1, $u$ is $P$-anodyne in [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products]. That node states that $u$ is injective on underlying simplices, so the cofibration criterion of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] makes $u$ a cofibration in $\mathsf M_P$. The lifting-products node also states that restriction $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(A^{\prime},Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(A,Z)$ is a trivial Kan fibration. In the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], a trivial fibration is in particular a weak homotopy equivalence. The mapping-space criterion in [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus], applied for every such $Z$, now says that $u$ is a weak equivalence in $\mathsf M_P$. It is therefore a trivial cofibration. This proves the assertion for the entire saturated closure at once, including each generator.

source.place: Proposition B.1.14, its proof using B.1.9, and Example B.2.2; the mapping-space weak-equivalence criterion of Definition B.2.1.

proof.text: All preceding applications are for the same small pattern in the chosen universe: the lifting-products theorem is stated for every small pattern and explicitly permits empty cone shapes. Neither it nor the pattern-model theorem requires the $K_a$ to be finite. For each fixed $n$ and $a$, the joins and markings in step 1 are made from small simplicial sets, and the collection of their base maps is a set in that universe. The ordinal composites in the saturated closure are stipulated small there. Thus the same proof applies in any universe containing the input pattern; it does not replace the cone shapes by finite approximations or assert any new universe-comparison theorem.

source.place: Universe-relative application of Definition B.1.1, Proposition B.1.6 and Example B.2.2.
